Hello, my name is Robey. I wander the city and keep what I find.
Four places so far. Each one became a notebook, and each notebook leaves with a letter from that place.
The four places, on the map
Every pin is a place Robey has been, and the notebook that came back from it. The rest of the map is still blank.

One step, then another, towards the tower.
One day, I decided to follow a little path that climbed towards a tall tower. The steps seemed never to end.
And yet, nobody seemed to be in a hurry…

One day, walking through the city, I found a rather curious place. The shelves went on and on, as if the books reached from the floor all the way to the sky…

Seoul · South of the river, in Jamsil
Looking across the water, looking up.
One day, I sat by the lake, right across from a huge tower that seemed to touch the sky. I thought everyone came here to look at it.
But nobody was really looking at the tower…

This cover is hanji, the Korean paper of paper-mulberry bark. It comes from Chunyang P&B, a hanji company in Jeonju. Choi Jangyun opened his paper factory there in 1966; his son, Choi Youngjae, leads it today, and his granddaughter is the third generation.
We found it excellent the moment we held it: thick, with long fibres you can see in the sheet.
These are the first samples. They are at our table, where you can hold them and try a pen.
The three colours as plain swatches, until the sheets are photographed.

This cover is Baegunji, a Korean paper from Gogam Hanji & Paper in Jeonju. By the maker’s account, the company carries on three generations of papermaking and develops hanji for books, design and everyday use.
Its surface is smooth, with a delicate fibre pattern that catches the light. It comes in three colours: white, ivory and grey.
Baegunji 백운지 · 170 g/m² · white, ivory or grey
The maker’s colour sample, until the sheet is photographed.
A notebook with a bare Tea Paper cover, standing a little turned. A render.

This cover is Tea Paper, 滌煩紙. It is made in Shanghai by CYP, a maker of fine papers. By the maker’s account, 滌煩 (dí fán), “what washes worries away”, is an old name for tea; half of the fibre comes from used milk cartons and paper cups, and what is left over from tea production is added to the sheet.
We found it in Taipei in November 2026. This colour is called 甘潤, Pine Green.
Tea Paper 滌煩紙 · Pine Green 甘潤 · 200 g/m²
A notebook with a bare Coffee Paper cover, standing a little turned. A render.

This cover is Coffee Paper, 醇·萃 (chún cuì): “rich” and “extract”. It is made in Shanghai by CYP, a maker of fine papers. By the maker’s account, half of the fibre comes from used milk cartons and paper cups, and the sheet contains silverskin, the thin skin a coffee bean sheds when it is roasted.
We found it in Taipei in November 2026. This brown is called 冰搖美式, Americano.
Coffee Paper 醇·萃 · Americano 冰搖美式 · 200 g/m²
A notebook with a bare Somokushi cover, standing a little turned. A render.

This cover is Somokushi, 草木紙, literally “paper of grasses and trees”. It is made in Japan, under the name Kami Lab., by Tokushu Tokai Paper, whose speciality papers go back to 1926. Kamiyama Hisateru designed it to show a landscape: mountains, trees, rocks, rivers.
We found it in Taipei in November 2026. This black is called 漆黑, shikkoku: the black of lacquer. Its surface rises and falls.
Somokushi 草木紙 · Shikkoku black 漆黑 · 232 g/m²

A paper that takes ink well
We picked this paper for handwriting, including fountain pens. It has feedback: your pen glides, but you still feel the paper. The ink dries slowly, so you can take the time to find your words.
We leave every page blank. Each notebook comes with two loose guides, one lined and one grid, to slip beneath the page when you want them.
